Course 11

Sleep and the mind

Why we sleep, what happens in each stage, how it affects mood and which habits really help.

Lesson 1. Why we sleep

1 · Lesson

We spend about a third of our lives asleep, and it is not wasted time. During sleep the brain consolidates what was learned during the day, regulates emotions, adjusts hormones and takes part in maintenance and clearance of brain tissue itself.

Sleep depends on two processes. The circadian clock, located in the hypothalamus and set mainly by light, keeps a rhythm of about 24 hours. Sleep pressure builds the longer we are awake, partly through the build-up of adenosine, and is released by sleeping.

Most adults need between seven and nine hours, though individuals vary. Regularly sleeping too little is associated with poorer attention, more irritability, more accidents and a higher risk of several physical and mental health problems.

2 · Example

Caffeine works partly by blocking adenosine receptors: it masks the tiredness signal but does not remove it. That is why, when it wears off, the accumulated sleep pressure returns, and a mid-afternoon coffee can delay sleep that night.

3 · Activity

For one week, write down when you go to bed, when you get up and how you feel on waking, from 1 to 5. At the end, see whether your better days match any pattern in your schedule.
